name: Ziyang Meng

papers.title: One-Step World Models for Multi-Modal Goal Navigation
papers.abstract: World-model-based planning is a promising direction for robot navigation because it enables explicit prediction of future observations under candidate actions. However, existing navigation world models typically rely on multi-step diffusion and autoregressive frame generation, which substantially increases model-side latency and complicates closed-loop deployment. In this work, we present a lightweight one-step world model for navigation built on a 3D U-Net with efficient spatial-temporal attention. The model predicts all future frames non-autoregressively in a single pass, while pretraining and random trajectory sampling improve performance in limited-data settings. We integrate this world model into a unified planning framework that supports image-goal, language-goal, and point-goal navigation through modality-specific scoring functions and anchor-based trajectory initialization. Extensive closed-loop experiments in both simulation and real-world environments show that the proposed approach improves generation efficiency and achieves strong navigation performance against state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: MosaicIMU: Composing Carrier Experts for Generalizable Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.abstract: Robust inertial odometry is essential for various carriers when external sensing is unreliable. Learning-based methods reduce integration drift by capturing local motion priors, but these methods often remain tied to a particular carrier, limiting generalization across heterogeneous platforms. We present MosaicIMU, a carrier-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) pretraining-and-adaptation framework for generalizable neural inertial odometry. MosaicIMU uses a prototype-based router to compose carrier-specific expert features, decodes local velocity and uncertainty constraints, and integrates them with a history-aware EKF. For unseen domain adaptation, it freezes the pretrained base model and learns a new lightweight expert residual branch. For edge-deployment, it further reuses the router to select informative online samples for efficient incremental updates. Experiments show that MosaicIMU consistently outperforms learning-based baselines, reducing average ATE and RTE-10s by 40% and 34%, respectively. These results highlight that MosaicIMU provides a scalable pretraining-to-deployment paradigm for generalizable and adaptive neural inertial odometry.
